parts.text: The Llesis family drove and hiked 6.5 hours to their vacation spot.
They drove an average of 50 miles per hour and hiked an average of 5 miles per hour less than half their speed when they drive.
If it took them 1.5 hours to hike, how far was their vacation spot?

parts.text: James gets 80 emails a day.
20% of those emails don't require any response.
He responds to the rest of them.
On Fridays, however, he gets twice as many emails, but still, 20% of them don't require any response.
How many emails does he respond to in a 5 day work week, considering that the number of emails he receives on Friday is doubled?

parts.text: Carlos, Jim, and Carrey were at the beach playing and they decided to gather some seashells.
Jim collected 27 seashells, which was 5 more than what Carlos collected.
Carlos collected twice as many as Carrey.
In the midst of their collection, a seagull swooped down and stole 3 seashells from Jim, but then a friendly beachcomber found 3 seashells and gave them back to Jim.
After all these events, they gathered all their seashells and divided them equally between themselves.
How many did each person get?

parts.text: Joe initially has twice as many cars as Robert.
He sells 20% of them and gives away twice as many cars as the number he sold to his mother.
After this, he buys 10 more cars and sells 5% of his total cars.
If Robert has 20 cars, how many cars does Joe remain with after selling, giving some to his mother, and buying more cars?

parts.text: Cayley markets various newspapers to get a commission on each copy sold.
He gets a 10% commission on each copy of the New York Times and an 8% commission on each of the Wall Street Journal.
Every time more than five copies are sold, an additional 1% commission is earned on each copy.
How much commission will he earn in total from the sales of 6 copies of the New York Times and 10 copies of Wall Street Journal if each costs $5 and $15 respectively?
